excerpt: Voiceops analyses customer phone calls with AI for B2C companies, surfacing coaching, compliance and product insights. Funding, use cases and alternatives.
content:
Voiceops is an AI platform that analyses customer phone calls for consumer-facing (B2C) businesses. Its site says most data tells you what happened while customer conversations tell you why, and the product listens to calls, extracts patterns and sends the findings to the people who can act on them. A feature it calls Synthesis pushes those insights into a team's existing workflows.

The uses Voiceops lists are practical: finding the tactics of top-performing reps so others can copy them, seeing how customers react to messaging, spotting competitor mentions and product gaps, flagging compliance problems and highlighting customers at risk of leaving. In a case study on its site, Truehold says its quality-assurance coverage went from about 2% of calls to 100%, and first-call conversion from 31% to 51%. These are the customer's and company's own figures.

In March 2025 Voiceops announced a $5 million seed round co-led by Bonfire Ventures and Twelve Below, with Precursor Ventures, Not Boring Capital, Village Global, Kearny Jackson, Mana Ventures and Four Acres Capital taking part, and former Airbnb executive Varsha Rao investing as an angel. The company said the money would go into product development, sales and marketing, and a new New York office. The announcement was written by Ethan Barhydt, who describes building earlier startups in the same space.

Voiceops does not publish prices; you book a demo. It says it can be set up in days. It is aimed at consumer-facing companies with sales or service teams that handle a high volume of calls, rather than at individuals.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
